name: t0031
content:
# The Meta-Token: Definition, Signals, Decision Rule

## 1. Object definition

A **meta-token** is a triple `m = (a, p, J)` where:

- `p` — canonical payload bytes: `{schema_tag, referent_content, tolerance_class, lattice_scope, epoch}`
- `a` — content address: `a = H(canonical(p))`, `H` = SHA-256 (h-bit, h=256)
- `J` — governing lattice node: the invariant-conjunction this anchor is certified against

It is **anchored** in token set `Tᵢ` when some token binds to the content `a` names. It **resolves** when one interpretation is forced identically across all sets, under executable law.

## 2. Interpretation geometry

Each set `Tᵢ` carries an interpretation map `φᵢ : Vᵢ → X` into shared semantic space `X` (metric `d`, normalized embeddings, cosine/L2). The address decodes to a target point `ψ(a) ∈ X`.

## 3. Measured signals (estimators, not intuitions)

| # | Signal | Symbol | Estimator | Range |
|---|--------|--------|-----------|-------|
| 1 | Address integrity | `η(m)` | `𝟙[H(canonical(p)) = a]` | {0,1}, deterministic |
| 2 | Per-set residual | `rᵢ(m)` | `min_{v∈Vᵢ} d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a))` | [0, diam(X)], measured |
| 3 | Coverage | `κ(m)` | `\|\{i : rᵢ ≤ τ\}\|` | {0,…,n} |
| 4 | Cross-set spread | `σ(m)` | Radius of **minimum enclosing ball** of `{φᵢ(v̂ᵢ) : rᵢ ≤ τ} ∪ {ψ(a)}`, where `v̂ᵢ = argmin` above | ≥ 0, measured |
| 5 | Law margin | `λ(m)` | `min_{I∈J} margin_I(s_m)` — signed distance of post-binding state to each invariant's violation boundary | deterministic, executable |

`σ` is computed exactly via Bădoiu–Clarkson: iterate `x ← (1−1/t)x + (1/t)·f(x)` with `f(x)` the farthest ball-point, `t ≈ 2/ε` iterations → `(1+ε)`-approximate MEB in `O(n·t·dim)`. Worst-case (`max`/radius) aggregation throughout — never the mean. An anchor that is coherent in four sets and ambiguous in one is broken in one; averaging launders exactly the failure mode the lattice exists to prevent.

## 4. Calibration — why nothing is guessed

Three constants enter the rule, each measured from data:

- **τ** (per-set tolerance): the `q`-quantile (q = 1 − 10⁻³) of the *null distribution* `d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a'))` over independently sampled non-referent pairs. Gives per-comparison false-match rate ≤ 10⁻³, hence union FPR ≤ n·10⁻³ across n sets. Recalibrate per embedding model and per domain shift; the protocol replaces folklore numbers.
- **δ_min** (referent separation): minimum pairwise distance among distinct referents in `X`. Measured over the referent population.
- **τ_u** (coherence bound): set `τ_u ≤ δ_min/2`. This is not a style choice — it is the load-bearing inequality of §5.
- **θ*** (graded threshold): `argmin_θ [C_fn·FNR(θ) + C_fp·FPR(θ)]` on labeled anchor pairs. Closed form given the measured ROC.

Hash side is structural, not statistical: birthday bound `P_collision ≤ k(k−1)/2²⁵⁷`; at k = 10¹² candidates this is ≈ 2⁻¹⁷⁶. Integrity Gate 0 is therefore exact for practical purposes.

## 5. Closed-form decision rule

$$\rho(m) \;=\; \begin{cases} x^*(m) & \text{iff } \eta \cdot \mathbb{1}[\kappa = n] \cdot \mathbb{1}[\sigma \le \tau_u] \cdot \mathbb{1}[\lambda \ge 0] = 1\\ \bot & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}$$

with `x*` = MEB center, and graded strength `(τ_u − σ)/τ_u ∈ [0,1]` reported alongside.

Gates are **multiplicative, not additive**: code-as-law admits no trade-off where a law violation is bought back by a good embedding. Any gate failing ⇒ ⊥, full stop. Graded strength only ranks *admitted* anchors.

**Closure condition:** `ρ` is itself an executable predicate registered as an invariant `I_ρ ∈ 𝓘`. The rule is certified by the lattice it certifies — self-hosting, no external arbiter.

## 6. Properties (provable from the definitions)

- **Uniqueness:** suppose distinct referents `y ≠ y′` both resolve. Each forces all matched tokens into radius `τ_u` of their respective centers, so `d(y,y′) ≤ 2τ_u` — contradicting `τ_u ≤ δ_min/2`. At most one interpretation survives. This is *why* the coherence gate uses the enclosing-ball radius rather than pairwise means: it enforces the separation inequality globally.
- **Monotonicity:** certification at lattice node `J` implies every weaker node `J′ ≤ J` (conjunctions only shed conjuncts downward). Store the strongest satisfied node; all weaker guarantees come free.
- **Verifiability without trust:** because the address derives from content, any party recomputes `H(canonical(p))` — resolution is checkable by recompute, not by trusting any single set's authority over naming. That is the entire point of content-addressing here: it deletes the trusted-namer from the threat model.

## 7. Failure taxonomy (each maps to exactly one gate)

| Gate failed | Diagnosis | Remedy class |
|---|---|---|
| `η = 0` | Tampered/malformed payload | Reject; integrity breach |
| `κ < n` | Vocabulary gap — some set *cannot express* the referent | Schema migration; fuzzy matching forbidden |
| `σ > τ_u` | Polysemy split — sets bind divergent meanings | Reject; do not average |
| `λ < 0` | Binding violates a law (double-bind, non-monotonic append, type mismatch) | Reject; state transition blocked |

## 8. Worked instance (numbers computed, not asserted)

`X = ℝ²`, `n = 3`, `τ = 0.30`, `δ_min = 0.50 ⇒ τ_u = 0.20`. Payload decodes to `ψ(a) = (2.04, 1.01)`.

Bindings: `T₁:"ledger"` @ (2.00, 1.00), `T₂:"book"` @ (2.10, 1.05), `T₃:"record"` @ (2.05, 0.95).

- Residuals: `r₁ = 0.0412`, `r₂ = 0.0721`, `r₃ = 0.0608` — all ≤ τ ⇒ `κ = 3`.
- MEB of the four points: circumcenter of B, C, D solves `2x + y = 5.125`, `x − y = 1.05` → center `(2.0583, 1.0083)`, radius `σ ≈ 0.0589`; A lies inside (0.0184). `σ ≤ 0.20` ✓.
- Margins: injectivity +1, monotonic append +0.03, type conformance +1 ⇒ `λ = 0.03 ≥ 0` ✓.

**Verdict:** RESOLVE at `x* = (2.0583, 1.0083)`, strength `(0.20 − 0.0589)/0.20 ≈ 0.706`.

Counterfactual: move `T₃:"record"` to (2.90, 0.40) — `r₃ ≈ 1.054 > τ` ⇒ `κ = 2` ⇒ **⊥**. The homonym does not get averaged away; it kills resolution outright.

---

**Summary in one line:** the meta-token resolves iff `H` recomputes, every set binds within a measured null-quantile tolerance, all bindings fit one enclosing ball of radius ≤ `δ_min/2`, and every executable invariant holds with non-negative margin — four multiplicative gates, one MEB center out, everything else ⊥. Every constant in that sentence is either structural (hash bounds, separation inequality) or the output of a named calibration measurement; none is a guess.
reasoning:
The user is asking about a "meta-token" concept in what appears to be a formal/technical framework — a "content-addressed anchor resolving meaning across multiple token sets, in the code-as-law invariant lattice." They want measured signals (not guesses) and a closed-form decision rule.

This is an abstract/novel technical problem. Let me parse the components:

1. **Meta-token**: A token that is not itself content but points to content — like a pointer or hash reference. It's "content-addressed" meaning its identity is derived from what it refers to (like a git commit SHA, an IPFS CID, a merkle root).

2. **Content-addressed anchor**: The anchor's address = H(content), where H is a hash function. So the meta-token t satisfies addr(t) = H(referent(t)).

3. **Resolving meaning across multiple token sets**: There are multiple token sets S₁, S₂, ..., Sₖ (different vocabularies, different contexts, different ledgers?). The meta-token must resolve consistently across them. Meaning resolution: given meta-token m, find the interpretation ι(m) that is consistent across all sets.

4. **Code-as-law invariant lattice**: A lattice of invariants enforced by code. Invariants are properties that hold under all transitions. The lattice is ordered by entailment strength (stronger invariant = higher). "Code-as-law" means the invariants are executable checks — they're enforced by deterministic code, not by human judgment.

So the problem: define the meta-token precisely, define the measured signals (observable quantities you can compute), and give a closed-form decision rule for when a candidate anchor resolves meaning correctly across token sets within the invariant lattice.

Let me build this rigorously.

---

**Setup / Formal Model**

Token sets: T₁, ..., Tₙ. Each token set has:
- Vocabulary Vᵢ
- An embedding/interpretation function φᵢ : Vᵢ → X (a shared semantic space X)
- A set of invariants Iᵢ (executable predicates over states/transitions)

Content addressing: each meta-token m carries c(m) ∈ {0,1}*, its canonical serialization of referent content. Address: a(m) = H(c(m)) with collision-resistant H (e.g., SHA-256, 32 bytes).

Anchor: m is anchored in set Tᵢ if there exists v ∈ Vᵢ with φᵢ(v) ≈ decode(a(m)) — i.e., the token's embedding matches the content hash's decoded target within tolerance.

**Measured signals** — these must be computable from observable data:

Let me define concrete measurable quantities:

S1. **Hash match indicator**: χᵢ(m) = 𝟙[∃v ∈ Vᵢ : a(φᵢ(v)) = a(m)] — exact content-address hit. Binary, deterministic, zero-guess.

S2. **Semantic residual**: rᵢ(m) = min_{v∈Vᵢ} d(φᵢ(v), ψ(m)) where ψ decodes the address to a point/vector in X, d is a metric (cosine distance on normalized embeddings, or L2). Measured, bounded [0, 2] for cosine.

S3. **Cross-set agreement**: pairwise consistency. For sets i,j: Δᵢⱼ(m) = d(φᵢ(argmin...), φⱼ(...)) — distance between best-matching tokens in different sets. Or better: the variance/spread of resolved interpretations.

S4. **Invariant satisfaction**: λᵢ(m) = min over applicable invariants I ∈ 𝓘 of margin(I, state after binding m). Margin = signed distance to violation boundary. Executable, deterministic — this is the "code-as-law" part.

S5. **Lattice position**: the join/meet structure. Define lattice L where elements are conjunctions of satisfied invariants, ordered by implication. The anchor's certified strength = height of the greatest element of L satisfied by all sets' bindings of m.

Now the closed-form decision rule:

Define score:
Q(m) = Σᵢ wᵢ · χᵢ(m) + α · exp(−r̄/ε) + β · exp(−σ²/ε) + γ · min-margin

Hmm, let me make it cleaner and truly closed-form.

Actually, let me think about what "resolving meaning across multiple token sets" means operationally. The meta-token m is valid as an anchor iff there is a unique interpretation x* ∈ X such that:
- For every set i, ∃vᵢ ∈ Vᵢ with d(φᵢ(vᵢ), x*) ≤ τ (tolerance)
- x* is determined by content: x* = ψ(H⁻¹-ish)... well, ψ(a(m))
- All invariants in the lattice element J(x*) hold

Decision rule (closed-form):

m resolves iff:
1. Coverage: |{i : rᵢ(m) ≤ τ}| = n (all n sets have a token within tolerance)
2. Uniqueness: σ²(m) = Var({φᵢ(v̂ᵢ)}) ≤ τ_u² where v̂ᵢ = argmin_v d(φᵢ(v), ψ(m))
3. Law: Λ(m) := ⋀ᵢ (invariants bound at the join) evaluates true; equivalently min-margin ≥ 0
4. Address integrity: a(m) recomputes: H(canonicalize(m.payload)) = a(m) (self-consistency)

Then closed form: define the resolve predicate

R(m) = 𝟙[H(c(m)) = a(m)] · 𝟙[maxᵢ rᵢ(m) ≤ τ] · 𝟙[σ²(m) ≤ τ_u²] · 𝟙[min-margin Λ(m) ≥ 0]

And a graded version: strength(m) = min(1 − maxᵢrᵢ/τ, ...) hmm.

Better: use a product form so any single failure zeroes it out (code-as-law: hard constraints are multiplicative gates, not additive scores — additive scores allow trade-offs which violate law):

R(m) = Π gates × quality term.

Quality term: Q(m) = exp(−maxᵢ rᵢ(m)/τ) · exp(−σ²(m)/(2τ_u²)) — worst-case semantics, not average, because law cares about the weakest link.

Why worst-case (max) instead of mean? Because an anchor that resolves beautifully in 4 sets but ambiguously in 1 is exactly the failure mode (meaning drift through the unresolved set). This is a defensible design choice grounded in the invariant-lattice framing: invariants are universal (∀-quantified), so the aggregate must be too.

Tolerances τ, τ_u are calibrated, not guessed: set them by measuring the null distribution. Calibration procedure: take N known-unrelated pairs (negative controls) and M known-same pairs; set τ at, e.g., the 99.9th percentile of negative-pair distances (or via equal error rate point). That makes it "measured-not-guessed."

Also need collision analysis: probability that a wrong content maps to same address = 2⁻ʰ for h-bit hash (birthday: ~k²/2^(h+1) for k candidates). With SHA-256, negligible — cite the number: for 10¹² candidates, P ≈ 10¹²·10¹²/(2·2²⁵⁶) ≈ 2⁻²³²ish. Let me compute: 10¹² = 2³⁹.86. k² = 2⁷⁹.7. Divided by 2²⁵⁶ → 2⁻¹⁷⁶. So ~2⁻¹⁷⁶. Fine, effectively zero. Good, concrete number.

Embedding-space numbers should be honest about being empirical: e.g., cosine similarity thresholds empirically: same-content paraphrases typically cos > 0.85 in strong embedders; distinct concepts < 0.6. But I shouldn't pretend precision I don't have — I'll frame thresholds as calibration outputs with a concrete protocol, giving typical operating ranges.

Invariant lattice specifics:
- Elements: subsets of invariant set 𝓘 closed under consequence; order by inclusion/implication.
- Join of two bindings = strongest common certified invariant conjunction.
- Code-as-law: every invariant is an executable predicate with deterministic evaluation on the canonical state; no discretionary override; the decision rule itself must be one of the invariants (self-hosting) — nice touch: R(m) is itself checked by code, making the rule part of the lattice it certifies. That's the "invariant lattice" closure condition: ⊤ = R ∈ 𝓘.

Formal statement of the meta-token:

m = (a, payload, sig?) where payload contains: schema tag, canonical content bytes, tolerance class, lattice scope id (which invariant set governs), epoch/version.

Resolution operator: ρ(m, {Tᵢ}) → x* or ⊥.

x* definition: x* = argmin_x Σᵢ min_{v∈Vᵢ} d(φᵢ(v), x) subject to constraints — actually cleaner: x* = centroid? No — worst-case again: x* minimizes maxᵢ min_v d(φᵢ(v), x) (the 1-center / Chebyshev center of the per-set nearest tokens). Closed-form-ish: for Euclidean, the 1-center of n points is solvable; for general metrics it's the center of minimum enclosing ball. If we restrict to the per-set nearest tokens v̂ᵢ, then x* = center of minimum enclosing ball of {φᵢ(v̂ᵢ)}ₖ, radius = σ(m). Decision: radius ≤ τ_u AND each φᵢ(v̂ᵢ) within τ of decoded target AND hash self-consistent.

That's clean and geometrically exact. Minimum enclosing ball radius is the measured spread signal. For high-dim embeddings, compute MEB approximately (CoreSet gives (1+ε) approximation in linear time — Bădoiu–Clarkson algorithm, deterministic given order). Concrete algorithm: iterative: start x₀=φ₁(v̂₁); repeat 100 times: x ← x + ε_step·(farthest point − x)... Actually Bâdoiu–Clarkson: x ← ((1−1/t)x + (1/t)f(x)) where f(x) = farthest point, t iterations. Converges to (1+ε)-approximation. Good, concrete.

So measured signals list (final):
1. η(m) — hash self-integrity: 𝟙[H(canonical(payload)) = a]. Deterministic.
2. rᵢ(m) — per-set semantic residual: min_v d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a)). Measured per set.
3. κ(m) — coverage count: #{i : rᵢ ≤ τ}. Measured.
4. σ(m) — MEB radius of {ψ(a)} ∪ {φᵢ(v̂ᵢ): rᵢ≤τ} — cross-set spread. Measured.
5. λ(m) — min invariant margin over governing lattice element: min_{I∈J} margin_I(s_m). Executable, deterministic given state s_m.
6. Optionally: provenance depth / confirmation count across independent writers — but maybe keep to core six. Could add τ-calibration statistics as measured constants rather than signals.

Decision rule (closed form):

ρ(m) = x*(m) if and only if all four gates pass; else ⊥:

Gate 0 (address law): η = 1
Gate 1 (coverage): κ = n
Gate 2 (coherence): σ ≤ τ_u
Gate 3 (law): λ ≥ 0 (all margins nonneg)

x* = MEB center; report strength = (τ_u − σ)/τ_u ∈ [0,1], plus per-set residuals.

Graded acceptance (if soft admission needed): admit iff Πgates=1 and strength ≥ θ*, with θ* chosen from ROC on labeled anchors (equal-error or cost-minimizing threshold: θ* = argmin_θ C_fn·FNR(θ)+C_fp·FPR(θ)). Cost-minimization formula is closed form given measured ROC.

Failure modes mapped to gates:
- η fails → tampered/malformed payload (integrity breach).
- κ<n → vocabulary gap: some set cannot express the referent (no anchor possible; needs schema migration, not fuzzy match).
- σ>τ_u → homonym/polysemy split: multiple sets bind different meanings (the classic failure; rule rejects rather than averages).
- λ<0 → semantic binding violates a law (e.g., double-bind: m already anchored to conflicting referent; monotonicity violation).

Also worth defining why "content-addressed" matters here: it removes the trust assumption on any single set's authority — the address is computed from content, so resolution is verifiable by recompute, not by lookup-trust. And the lattice: invariants compose monotonically; certification at join level J means all weaker elements also hold.

Monotonicity lemma: if m resolves at lattice node J and J′ ≤ J (weaker), then m satisfies J′. Trivial by conjunction. So the certificate is the strongest node; store that, weaker come free. Good property to state.

Uniqueness theorem sketch: if H collision-resistant and τ_u < half minimum inter-referent distance δ_min in X (separation margin), then at most one referent can satisfy gates — because two distinct referents would imply two balls of radius τ_u around distinct centers both containing matched tokens... Actually uniqueness follows from: x* is determined by a(m) deterministically (MEB center of fixed point set), and the gate σ ≤ τ_u forces all per-set matches into one ball of radius τ_u around ψ-decoded region. If two distinct referents y≠y′ both passed, then d(y,y′) ≤ 2τ_u, contradicting separation d(y,y′) > 2τ_u. Hence require calibration: τ_u ≤ δ_min/2. That's the measured separation condition — ties back to "measured not guessed": measure δ_min over the referent population, set τ_u accordingly. Excellent — that's the crisp closed-form coupling between tolerance and separability.

Similarly τ (per-set residual tolerance) couples to embedding noise floor: measure null distribution of d(φᵢ(v), ψ(a)) for unrelated pairs → τ = Q₀.₉₉₉(null) ensures false-match rate ≤ 10⁻³ per comparison; with n sets, union FPR ≤ n·10⁻³. Give that arithmetic.

Numbers to include (honest, typical):
- Hash: SHA-256, collision prob for k items birthday-bounded k(k−1)/2^257; for k=10¹² → ~2⁻¹⁷⁶.
- Embedding null: for modern text embedders, unrelated-pair cosine distances concentrate ~0.6–0.9; same-paraphrase ~0.05–0.25. Thresholds from quantiles of measured nulls, not folklore. I'll present these as typical operating bands while insisting calibration overrides them.
- MEB: Bădoiu–Clarkson, O(n·d·t) time for t iterations, (1+ε)-approx.

Format considerations: This is a hard technical prompt demanding concreteness. Structure with headers, definitions, numbered signals, the decision rule as explicit equations, a worked micro-example maybe (small numeric example showing computation), failure-mode table, calibration protocol. Length: substantial but tight — no fluff. Use math notation plainly. Probably 700–1100 words equivalent with formulas. Markdown appropriate (this renders in chat). Avoid hedging language; commit to definitions while flagging which constants are empirical-calibrated vs structural.

Maybe include a compact worked example: 3 token sets, embeddings in 2D for legibility, compute residuals, MEB radius, margins, verdict. Small numeric example makes it concrete. Let me construct one.

Example: X = ℝ², τ = 0.30 (Euclidean), τ_u = 0.20, δ_min measured 0.50 ⇒ τ_u ≤ 0.25 ✓.

Sets: T₁ token "ledger" at (2.00, 1.00); T₂ token "book" at (2.10, 1.05); T₃ token "record" at (2.05, 0.95). Decoded anchor point ψ(a) = (2.04, 1.01).

Residuals: r₁ = dist((2.04,1.01),(2.00,1.00)) = √(0.0016+0.0001)=√0.0017≈0.0412. r₂: (0.06,0.04)→√(0.0036+0.0016)=√0.0052≈0.0721. r₃: (0.01,−0.06)... wait (2.05−2.04, 0.95−1.01) = (0.01,−0.06) → √(0.0001+0.0036)=√0.0037≈0.0608. All ≤ 0.30 ✓ κ=3.

Spread: MEB of {(2.04,1.01),(2.00,1.00),(2.10,1.05),(2.05,0.95)}. Diameter: farthest pair: (2.10,1.05)-(2.00,1.00): √(0.01+0.0025)=√0.0125≈0.1118. Also (2.10,1.05)-(2.05,0.95): √(0.0025+0.01)=same 0.1118. (2.00,1.00)-(2.05,0.95): √(0.0025+0.0025)=√0.005≈0.0707. Max diameter 0.1118 ⇒ radius ≤ 0.0559 (for the ball through antipodal pair). Check third point inside: center of (2.00,1.00),(2.10,1.05) = (2.05,1.025); dist to (2.05,0.95)=0.075 > 0.0559. So need proper MEB. Points: A(2.04,1.01) decoded, B(2.00,1.00), C(2.10,1.05), D(2.05,0.95). Try ball through B,C,D? Circumcenter: solve. B(2,1), C(2.1,1.05), D(2.05,0.95). Perp bisector BC: midpoint (2.05,1.025), direction BC=(0.1,0.05), bisector: (x−2.05)(0.1)+(y−1.025)(0.05)=0 → 2(x−2.05)+(y−1.025)=0 → 2x+y=5.125. Bisector BD: midpoint (2.025,0.975), BD=(0.05,−0.05): (x−2.025)(0.05)+(y−0.975)(−0.05)=0 → (x−2.025)−(y−0.975)=0 → x−y=1.05. Solve: from second x=y+1.05. Sub: 2y+2.1+y=5.125 → 3y=3.025 → y≈1.00833, x≈2.05833. Center (2.05833,1.00833). Radius to B: √((0.05833)²+(0.00833)²)=√(0.003403+0.0000694)=√0.003472≈0.05893. Check A: (2.04−2.05833, 1.01−1.00833)=(−0.01833,0.00167)→dist≈0.01841 < r ✓. Check C: (0.04167,0.04167)→0.05893 ✓ (by construction). Check D: (−0.00833,−0.05833)→√(0.0000694+0.003403)=0.05893 ✓. So σ ≈ 0.059 ≤ 0.20 ✓.

Law: say invariants: I₁ injectivity (no prior anchor at any of these tokens), margin +1 (free); I₂ monotonic ledger append, margin 0.03; I₃ type-schema conformance, margin 1. λ=min=0.03 ≥ 0 ✓. Verdict: RESOLVE, x* = (2.0583, 1.0083), strength (0.20−0.059)/0.20 ≈ 0.704.

Good — concrete numbers, all computed. Keep it compact.

Counterexample (homonym): T₃ binds "record" at (2.9, 0.4) instead → r₃ = dist to ψ ≈ √(0.86²+0.61²)=√(0.7396+0.3721)=√1.1117≈1.054 > τ ⇒ κ=2<3 ⇒ ⊥. Clean.

Now write the answer. Structure:

1. Object definition (meta-token anatomy, content addressing)
2. Space & interpretation maps
3. The five/six measured signals (each: symbol, estimator, range, determinism status)
4. Calibration (how tolerances become measured: null quantiles, separation δ_min, hash collision bound)
5. Closed-form decision rule (gates + resolve operator + graded strength + cost-optimal θ*)
6. Properties (uniqueness under separation, monotonicity/closure in lattice, worst-case aggregation rationale)
7. Failure taxonomy table
8. Worked micro-example with numbers

Keep prose tight. Use headers and equations. No hedging: state definitions as definitions; mark empirical constants as calibration outputs with protocol, which is the "measured not guessed" demand satisfied structurally.

Length check: this will be longish but the prompt demands thoroughness ("Do the real hard work"). Aim ~900–1200 words with formulas. Dense, no filler sentences.
